items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: One of the thughest numbers I ever played was the arrangement of "Whitman Stomp" by Charlie Dickson, the Fletcher Henderson banjo player.

ctx.x: There was not much we could do on this long trip because there was no lounge car where we could play cards or some other games. Some of the stops in different cities would be as long as two or three hours, and there we had a chance to buy some juice which we would pass around amongst us and pray that we had enough to last until the next long stop. We bought quite a number of paper bag lunches as it would be hours between stops and there was no restaurant car on the train. There was a war going on and the most…

Kirby was engaged to play a month in a place called 'Burton's Lounges' and Burton's was one of the two clubs run by Negroes in Oakland. For one week, Buster Bailey and I got together on the Kirby book which I must admit was one of the toughest that I ever had to tackle. One of the thughest numbers I ever played was the arrangement of "Whitman Stomp" by Charlie Dickson, the Fletcher Henderson banjo player. But most of the numbers in Kirby's book were arranged by Charlie Shavers and Charlie was as touch an arranger…

We played a matinee every afternoon from five to seven, and from ten till two a.m. every night. There were plenty of sailors in town, because there was a naval base near Oakland. So the town and the joints were jumping. The prostitutes were getting rich and hinkty. Even those that looked like Wolephant had their asses on their shoulders. Wolephant is the name Arvell Shaw, the bass player, called ugly chicks, a mixture of wolf and elephant.
